theory.md: A market is **efficient** if prices already contain the available information. Then you cannot beat the market with that information, because it is already in the price.

head: Form
Information already in the price
What does not work any more

theory.md: Strong ⊃ semi-strong ⊃ weak. Each form includes the one below.

standardAnswer.md: The ==efficient market hypothesis== says that prices reflect all available information. In the ==weak form== prices contain all past prices, so ==technical analysis== cannot earn excess returns. In the ==semi-strong form== prices also contain all public information, so ==fundamental analysis== does not help. In the ==strong form== even private information is priced in, so not even insiders can earn abnormal returns.

tasks.name: Explain the strong form and test it
tasks.question: Explain the three forms of market efficiency. How could you test the **strong form**?

checklist.text: Definition: prices reflect all available information
Weak form: past prices → no technical analysis
Semi-strong: + public information → no fundamental analysis
Strong: + private information → no insider profits
Test: do insiders / fund managers earn abnormal returns?

modelAnswer.md: See the standard answer above. **Test of the strong form:** check whether insiders or professional fund managers earn ==abnormal returns==. If they do, the strong form is rejected.

cards.back:
- **Weak:** past prices
- **Semi-strong:** + public info
- **Strong:** + private info
